p2-h12.actual: GET /api/rota now cross-checks each shift's staffId against that day's approved absences (server/src/routes/rota.ts flagShiftsOnLeave/approvedLeaveByName, matched by name since absences.staffId is a name-slug, not the rota's own staff.id). Verified live: PUT /api/rota assigned a staffer to a shift; GET showed no flag; POST /api/leave/absences recorded approved leave covering that date; GET then showed needsCover:true and staffOnLeave:true on the same shift, with staffId unchanged (the assignment itself is never touched); cancelling the leave via POST /api/leave/absences/:id/cancel made the flag disappear on the next GET.
p2-h12.notes: This fix was already present on the branch (commit 0eb0317c, 'Overnight P3 testing pass') before this batch started — re-verified against the live API rather than re-implemented.

p2-h13.actual: PUT /api/availability/mine now bounds a dated grid submission against the window(s) actually requested for that staffer (server/src/routes/availability.ts): a camp request bounds by camp.startDate..+weeks*7-1, a week/range request bounds by window.from/to; a submission with any grid date outside every bound is refused 400 before anything is written. Verified live: POST /api/availability/requests created a 'week' request with from/to a week out; PUT /mine with a grid date 10 days past the window's end returned 400; PUT /mine with a grid date inside the window returned 200 and saved.
p2-h13.notes: An 'ongoing' request (no from/to) carries no bound, by design — it's a standing weekly pattern, not a dated one, so there's nothing to enforce against.
p2-h13.evidence: server/src/routes/availability.ts (PUT /mine); throwaway server/src/plan2BatchHRTest.mts (deleted after the run)

p2-l1.actual: POST /api/learning/completions reads the tenant's Setup -> Learning passMark (server/src/routes/learning.ts, via loadSettings, same convention as other Setup-configured thresholds) and refuses a score below it with 422 {code:'below_pass_mark'} instead of recording a completion; a passing score is stored with completed:true and the passMark it cleared. Verified live: PUT /api/library set settings.learning.passMark=90; a score of 70 was refused 422/below_pass_mark; a score of 95 was accepted 200, and the stored Firestore doc in learningCompletions carries completed:true, passMark:90, score:95.
p2-l1.notes: This fix was already present on the branch (commit 67f5ba1c, 'Plan 2 day 7: server-side pass mark on completions') before this batch started — re-verified against the live API rather than re-implemented. The POST/GET responses don't echo a literal `completed` field back to the client (only the stored doc carries it), but that's moot in practice: anything that clears the 422 gate is by definition >= passMark, so every completion that reaches the client is a real pass.
p2-l1.evidence: server/src/routes/learning.ts (doneSchema, POST /completions); throwaway server/src/plan2BatchHRTest.mts (deleted after the run)

p2-o6.actual: Built a real sweep, inventoryLowStock() in server/src/lib/sweeps.ts, registered once in startSweeps() (sweep('inventory-low-stock', 60*60_000, inventoryLowStock)) without touching any existing sweep. It scans the `inventory` collection for items at/below minQty with the tenant's Setup -> Inventory lowStockAlert flag on (default on, same rule the UI badge already used), and bells the tenant once per item via fireOnce (keyed by item id only, matching listingAutoExpire's convention) + notify({to:{kind:'tenant'}}) under a new 'inventory' NotifyCategory. Verified by calling the exported function directly against a seeded item (quantity 2, minQty 5): first call raised exactly one notification naming the item and its reorder level; a second call raised none (fireOnce dedup held).
p2-o6.notes: Added the 'inventory' category to NotifyCategory (server/src/lib/notify.ts) since none of the existing categories fit; it's tenant-audience only, not added to the parent-mute CATEGORIES list or STAFF_CATEGORIES (matches how 'listing' alerts are scoped). sweeps.ts had unrelated concurrent work in progress (an uncommitted onboarding-retention sweep) — left entirely untouched; only my inventoryLowStock function and its one registration line were added.
p2-o6.evidence: server/src/lib/sweeps.ts (inventoryLowStock, startSweeps); server/src/lib/notify.ts (NotifyCategory); throwaway server/src/plan2BatchHRTest.mts (deleted after the run)
